message: The new contract is for $850, with milestones organized by scene. I’ve also uploaded a revised script to the shared google folder; it has only a few small changes from the previous version. Since you don’t need to create the text cards, I’ll handle those myself. That may leave a little extra in funds for fine-tuning, although we’ll have to see how things go. Please let me know if anything is unclear. Thanks!
If any questions come up while I read through the script again, I’ll write to you.
Ok great
Ppl
Because the artistic style can gradually drift, please do everything possible to keep it consistent and get the intended look exactly right.
Before I proceed with the remaining work, I’ll generate an image and send it to you for approval.
I’m currently analyzing the SQ4 storyboard images. Should the video use color images or black-and-white ones?
For the video format, which orientation should I use: vertical or horizontal?
To reduce costs, storyboards are often kept in black and white; the final video, however, must be in full color.
Use a 9:16 aspect ratio with a vertical orientation.
For the first-scene video, I’m now sending a link containing key images created from the ones you supplied. Please review them and leave your comments.
The review materials are available through this shared-folder link: <https://drive.riverstone.example/folders/synthetic-folder-riverstone-4826?usp=sharing>
If you can, identify each suitable frame here by writing its name followed by "+". For any frame that needs changes, provide its name along with a comment specific to that frame.
The review notes were sent by email.

Resolution depends on the shot angle, and images taken from an angle this long cannot be improved beyond their current quality. Did you zoom in on the hero? Also, frames where the pulse moves do not always require many separate images, because the video already specifies how that should work.
Another revision of every image is what I’ll attempt next.
Using only photos of the characters and the location, we can create an alternative version of the video fragment without detailed photo frames. I’d like to show you that option as well.
During 0-14 seconds, your video shows footage from a height, but the script does not include it. Should shots like that be added?
Because these set images are the ones you supplied, their current quality represents the maximum improvement possible from those sources.

I hadn’t realized this limitation existed. Do low-angle shots automatically have lower resolution, while higher-angle shots can achieve better resolution? I’m fine with changing the shot angles whenever doing so improves the quality of the set images.
Let’s secure all the other required material before spending time on the opening aerial establishing shot. I still want that shot, but it has a lower priority than everything else we need.

My set images don’t seem high quality enough, and I hadn’t realized we would be limited to their existing resolution. Would generating new set images to use as starting frames improve the quality, and is that worth doing? I’m fine with that approach if it would help.
Despite being shown from a distant perspective, the hero is still marked in the image, even though his details are not visible.
The possibility that you’ll want to add a voiceover later is why I asked for clarification. We should account for that now when timing the shots.
Could I create similar backgrounds? The image setup does affect the resulting quality.
Would medium and close-up angles work in place of the current distant shots?
New sets are fine with me, provided they remain stylistically on point and consistent across the shots. If possible, though, I want to keep the long wide shots that open the sequence.
The framing moves from wide in the first set to mid in the second, then closer in the third.
Ok

Sorry—the confusion came from my using "set" in more than one sense. There are three PAIRS of images, and each pair contains 1 shot of Kestrel and 1 shot of Red Fern. In framing order, the first two images are long/wide, the second two images are mid, and the third pair is closer, showing them from the waist up.
To avoid doing the wrong job, can we review the details once more? I’ve already made the images a little better, but should we leave them like this with the background?
Would this long-angle approach for shot SQ4\_1 suit you? With this angle, the hero will usually not be in focus, while the frame remains on screen for a few seconds without zooming in.
Is this the angle for SQ4\_3?
Before I can rework the remaining shots, these revised ones need to be reconciled and reviewed. Some of the shots have already been reworked.
For review, I've shared the revised shots here: <https://drive.riverstone.example/folders/synthetic-folder-riverstone-4826?usp=drive_link>
For this image set, I sent the review notes by email.
I've gone through the notes—thanks. The sets are actually distinct; still, could they be quite similar, and would that level of similarity be appropriate?
Although they may look similar, the resulting sets are still different; all I did was improve the images you supplied, not replace them.
Compared with my originals, these revised sets are much more similar to one another.
Please review the materials in this shared folder: <https://drive.riverstone.example/folders/synthetic-folder-riverstone-4826?usp=sharing>
I've delivered the new images in this shared folder: <https://drive.riverstone.example/folders/synthetic-folder-riverstone-4826?usp=drive_link>
Thanks—the latest images look much better now. I've sent my review notes separately by email.
Following your notes, I revised the image and included a few new frames in this delivery: <https://drive.riverstone.example/folders/synthetic-folder-riverstone-4826?usp=drive_link>
Because I'm only scaling the Kestrel set and changing nothing else, I honestly don't understand why you don't like it.
Would it help if I sent the background and the character without the background as separate assets, so you can show me your preferred arrangement?
I'm scaling the image in Photoshop.
A perfect crop that retains the details you identified isn't possible with AI. I'll therefore do it manually, exactly as requested, using only Photoshop, and send you the result later.

Using Photoshop rather than AI, I completed the crop. You can review it here: <https://drive.riverstone.example/folders/synthetic-folder-riverstone-4826?usp=drive_link>. If it still isn't correct, I don't know another way to do it.

Overall, these look good, but a few small issues remain. The bridge behind Kestrel at his waste is badly placed; please remove it along with the bridge just above his head. To prevent the lower bridges from interfering, leave only the one upper bridge in the Kestrel images. The character shadows are also missing—can you restore them without changing anything else? Thanks for sticking with it!
What kind of shadows do you mean? Could you describe them in more detail?
Do you need only the characters' shadows?
Have images 14a, 14b, 16a,16b,16c been reviewed as well?
The character shadows visible in earlier renders are absent from these renders.
I’ll review the other images as well—sorry about that.

Please review the folder here: <https://drive.riverstone.example/folders/synthetic-folder-riverstone-4826?usp=drive_link>. I’ve added new SQ4-SQ9, along with new shots that you haven’t commented on yet. Thanks.

If possible, could you share all the requested changes together and in advance? Receiving adjustments piece by piece often means reworking everything from the beginning, which takes additional time. I’d really appreciate your understanding—thank you!
I’m confused because I’ve been following your storyboard strictly, yet the SQ11 script says the angle changed. I’m supposed to be guided by the storyboard, right?
For SQ12, has everything changed as well?

Additional work that wasn't initially anticipated can result when the script differs from the storyboard. To keep everything running smoothly, it would really help if the script matched the storyboard from the outset, or if any deviations were shared in advance. I just wanted to clarify that—thank you!

I agree—you’re totally right, and I apologize. I should have highlighted those changes more directly and updated the storyboard reel.

There aren’t any other significant changes like that, but I’ll review the script and explicitly identify any remaining small tweaks so we are 100% clear on the direction.

Sorry again; I’ll circle back with that information.
Before I continue, should SQ5, SQ7 be changed? Also, can you confirm whether SQ10 onwards match the storyboard?
Please pause for now while I compile a list of any other changes before you do more work, so we don’t waste effort. Because I’m traveling today, I can only send it tomorrow or the day after.
I want to identify each one specifically, even though only a few small tweaks remain.
Okay
While the other work is paused, you could keep going on SQ4 if you want, using my notes from yesterday about the energy blast.
When it comes to SQ11 and SQ12, I no longer understand which frames should be included or how many are required.
Before work resumes, please allow me a day. During that time, I’ll capture any and all changes and write a detailed description of the remaining shots in SQ4.

The script already specified the shot angles I wanted and explicitly noted that the storyboard angles were wrong. If you followed only the storyboard reel rather than the script, that explains why we misunderstood each other. Since I can’t reliably create images with the right angles to demonstrate them in the reel, what alternative process would work for you? How should I communicate each angle so you can render the shot correctly?
Despite spending hours trying to create images with the right angles, I’m still not getting the references I need. It’s becoming a huge waste of both time and energy...

Even when I focus exclusively on the script, the required frame counts for SQ4\_7 Mid-Shot, SQ4\_8 3⁄4 Mid Shot, SQ4\_9, SQ4\_11 remain unclear to me. Do all of those shots differ from your storyboard, and what exactly has changed?

Because I can produce the shots only according to how I interpret the written text, the results may not match what you are imagining, which can cause misunderstandings. Could you briefly describe the changes in your storyboard to make the intended shots clearer?
Here is the footage with the previous changes included; please review it at <https://drive.riverstone.example/folders/synthetic-folder-riverstone-4826?usp=drive_link>.
Without a storyboard, it’s difficult to determine exactly which frame you need. What do you think of this 20-frame option?

For every part that differs from the storyboard reel, I’ll identify the mismatch and provide a highly detailed shot description. Before generating any frames, you can ask whatever questions or request any clarifications you need.

Getting both the character details and the style I prefer has also been difficult. If I provide two images—one for character details and one for style—could you try generating an image that combines both aspects?

Because I’m not good at updating the storyboard reel yet and doing so takes me too long, I’d prefer to try more detailed shot descriptions, possibly supported by example frames I find online. Updating the reel myself remains an option as well.

To clarify, although I mentioned presenting still frames as a digital comic book, I want to attempt the animation first. I’ll fall back to the digital comic book with still frames only if the animation produces poor results or proves too difficult or expensive.
Okay—what should my next step be?
Please give me a day while I work on the full descriptions for shots that have changed from the storyboard and on the new character reference. Until then, there’s nothing for you to do.
We can discuss providing more funds if any of this seems to warrant them.

Rather than decide now whether to add more money, I’d prefer to revisit it at the end. I’m hoping the remaining sequences will get easier and move more quickly as we develop a good process. If, once everything is finished, the overall work turns out to be more than we planned, I’m happy to add more—I want to make sure you feel good about it.
Okay, I'll wait for your instructions. Have you watched the updated footage of SQ4-SQ10?

Everything looks fine so far regarding the cost of the image creation phase. Video creation will be the most expensive part, but I can’t assess that cost yet because we haven’t created any animation or discussed its style.
Hello! I hope everything is going well; could you let me know whether our work will be continuing?
Sorry—other things have kept me busy. I’ll send you the updated images tomorrow morning.

Let’s hold off on moving forward until we finesse the character style a bit. It keeps drifting, and I’ve struggled to keep it precise. Red Fern and Blue Lantern are close to the target; Kestrel is furthest away because he feels too clean, too simple, and too polished. What I want instead is more of a raw graffiti aesthetic. Could you do a quick pass applying that style to all three of them and send me the results?
More attitude comes through in this reference: it’s darker and rougher, with stronger sketch energy.
This is my favorite of the three because of his detail and features, so use it as the target if you need one.

I had been waiting for details about the scene, only for you to decide to change everything. Sorry, but that isn't how this is done: you gave me a script with characters and a storyboard, and I spent a lot of time creating an image using your previous images.
Sorry. Because I wasn't happy with how the characters looked, I asked about changes and offered to pay you more; you said that was fine, which is why I made the request and the offer.
For the work that needs to be redone, I'm still happy to pay.
Are you asking to change one hero? I'm concerned that he would look stylistically different from the others.
Okay. To work more productively on the project and reach the point where I can make your video, I need you to tell me what my next steps are.
What additional funds would you require for just one attempt at altering the style of all three characters, followed by recreating the frames as we currently have them?
If you want new heroes created, the price would be $45 per hero. Is that what you're asking for?
Since the character details are already dialed in and we have a target style, I had hoped this would be easier. Ah, okay—I'll try it on my own instead.
yes, okay
When do you think we’ll be able to resume work on the video? Hi—I hope you’ve been well.

Adrian, hi—I hope you’re doing well.

Since I’ll be taking some leave shortly, I’d like to coordinate everything in advance. Have you decided what you’d like to do with the heroes, and are you still planning to continue the project?

Thank you!

A burst pipe has made the house chaotic, and with preschool closed for staff training I’ve been juggling childcare all week. Sorry for the delayed reply.

I do want to proceed, and I have some new images, though nothing is final yet.

When do you leave for vacation, and how long will you be away?

I do want to continue…

Okay, I understand you. I will wait for information from you.

Vacation from 14.08 to 23.08
Adrian, I hope you’re doing well! Could you tell me where things stand with the work on the video?

If you could help refine the look a little and run a few more animation tests, I’d be game. At the moment, though, it mostly feels as if achieving the look I want would require more investment, and I might not be able to get the animation quality I want either. Unless I’m confident we can get there, I just can’t rationalize using up our contract on further look development or animation testing.
For the still frames we worked on in October, how much time did you spend?
To be honest, Adrian, I can’t recall exactly how much time I spent on the still frames we worked on in October.
Your explanation makes sense to me, so thank you. From here, how would you like to proceed?
